_licence.source: Runcible curated notation facts, written for this Book
_licence.note: Four closed sets: what a time signature counts, what a key signature names, what two letters are apart, and what three letters make. Each row is a fact of the notation stated in this site's own words. musictheory.net teaches the same four groups and grants no licence, so it stays a link in chapter 2 and nothing of its wording is here.

title: The four groups a scheduler can hold

fields.signature: the time signature as written, top over bottom. One string in both languages: a number over a number is the same in each.
fields.beats: how many of the note the lower number names fit in one bar. One string in both languages, because it is a numeral.
fields.written: the key signature counted in sharps or flats. { en, es }.
fields.key: the major key that signature names. { en, es }, because the Spanish half of this Book names notes in solfege and the page it sits under does too.
fields.relative: the minor key sharing the same signature. { en, es }. Shown after the answer, never asked.
fields.pair: two letters, low to high. { en, es }.
fields.interval: what they are apart. { en, es }.
fields.chord: the triad by name. { en, es }.
fields.notes: the accepted spellings of its three letters, low to high, spaces between. A list per language, because a sharp may be typed as # or as the word, and compare.js grades any member right. A typed answer is graded against the language on screen, so the Spanish list is the one a Spanish reader is marked against.

meter.note: Two quarter notes to a bar. March time, and the meter of Schumann's Soldier's March.
Three quarter notes to a bar. Every menuet in chapter 4 is in it.
Four quarter notes to a bar, and the one written as a C often enough that the C is worth recognising.
Two half notes to a bar. The same length as 4/4 and counted half as often, which is the whole point of writing it this way.
Three eighth notes to a bar. Clementi's third movement is in it.
Six eighth notes to a bar, and a player counts them as two beats of three. The number answers what is written; the feel is two.
Nine eighth notes, felt as three beats of three.
Twelve eighth notes, felt as four beats of three.
Five quarter notes. It does not divide evenly, so the composer usually says how to group them.
Six quarter notes. The same grouping question as 6/8, one note value slower.

keys.note: The only signature that prints nothing at all.
The sharp is F, and the sharps always arrive in the order F C G D A E B.
The flat is B, and the flats arrive in the order B E A D G C F, which is the sharps backwards.
B and E. Tchaikovsky's Old French Song is in the minor of this pair.

intervals.note: Two letters apart, four semitones. The bottom of a major triad.
Two letters apart, three semitones. The bottom of a minor triad.
Four letters apart, seven semitones. The outer notes of any plain triad.
Six letters apart, eleven semitones, one semitone short of the octave.
Twelve semitones, and the same letter again.
Two letters apart, three semitones. The same size as C to E flat and spelled with no accidental.
Four letters apart but only six semitones, because the white keys are not evenly spaced. The one fifth in the major scale that is not perfect.

triads.note: The third is F sharp, which is one of the two sharps D major carries. The other is C sharp, the seventh degree, and no triad on the tonic reaches it.
A minor third stacked on a minor third, so the fifth is diminished.
A major third stacked on a major third, so the fifth is augmented.
